title: A transferred count dispersion model gave no clear M6+ occurrence Brier score gain near 323 shallow M6.5+ centers in 2013-2024
abstract: We tested whether a count dispersion estimate fitted at M5.5 improves M6+ occurrence probabilities without a new dispersion fit. We used a fixed ComCat snapshot, 363 training centers in 2001-2012 and 323 test centers in 2013-2024. Centers have M6.5 or more and depth at most 70 km. Targets cover days 7-30 within 200 km. A negative-binomial transfer reduced Brier score from 0.09057 to 0.08753. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for gain was -0.00008 to 0.00648. The primary test gives no clear gain. Binary log score improved by 0.00995 nats, with limits 0.00172 to 0.01933. Mean occurrence probability fell from 16.80% to 14.94%, compared with 11.15% observed. Brier inference changed with block length. This extends known count-score evidence on the same test data. It does not establish a physical mechanism or operational forecast benefit. Revised records, shared windows, a common magnitude survival fraction, fixed-fit uncertainty and twelve test years limit inference. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, an independent audit and a figure are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Brier score gain after magnitude transfer. Bars show conditional three-year block intervals. Pooled M6+ probabilities remain above the observed fraction.

citations.reason: Published lower-threshold count benchmark motivates this higher-threshold transfer test. Samples overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
